title: Cap. 6 Arg. 5 close: Boasting cut off; glory of human salvation wholly God's
pass_a_gloss: Third, from our opinion it follows that every handle for boasting has been snatched away from human beings, and that the glory of human salvation is to be attributed wholly to God, who distinguishes human beings from human beings, according to that of the Apostle (1 Corinthians 4:7), "Who makes you to differ? What do you have that you did not receive?" "From whom," says Augustine, "except from him who distinguishes you from another, to whom he did not give what he gave to you?" (De praedestinatione sanctorum, chapter 9). But if their opinion should prevail who think that by Christ's death God has been made equally benevolent toward all human beings; and who maintain that from this equal propensity toward all grace is so administered that whoever uses the light of nature well, or whoever has done what is in him, draws it to himself; that whoever uses the same light badly, or has not done what is in him, does not draw it—then he who has come out a partaker of grace has from himself a just matter of boasting, because by his own choice he distinguished himself from him from whom he was not distinguished by any special gift of divine mercy.
pass_b_english: Third, our view leaves human beings no handle for boasting, and assigns the glory of human salvation wholly to God, who makes one person differ from another—as the Apostle says: "Who makes you differ? What do you have that you did not receive?" (1 Corinthians 4:7). "From whom," Augustine asks, "except from him who distinguishes you from another, to whom he did not give what he gave you?" (De praedestinatione sanctorum 9). But if their view wins—that by Christ's death God has become equally kind to all people, and that from this equal bent toward all he administers grace so that whoever uses nature's light well, or does what lies in him, draws grace to himself, while whoever uses that light badly, or fails to do what lies in him, does not—then the person who ends up sharing in grace has from himself a fair ground of boasting: by his own choice he set himself apart from another whom no special gift of divine mercy had set apart.
source_text: Tertio, ex nostra sententia sequitur omnem gloriandi ansam praereptam esse hominibus, & gloriam salutis humanae Deo, qui homines ab hominibus discernit, esse totaliter tribuendam, juxta illud Apostoli, 1 Cor. iv. 7, Quis te discernit? quid habes quod non accepisti? A quo, inquit Augustinus, nisi ab illo qui te discernit ab alio, cui non donavit quod donavit tibi? De praed. Sanct. cap. 9. At si obtineat illorum sententia, qui morte Christi Deum erga universos homines ex aequo benevolum factum opinantur; atque ex hac aequali propensione erga omnes gratiam sic administrari tuentur, ut eam ad se trahat quisquis bene utatur lumine naturae, aut quisquis fecerit quod in se est; non trahat, quisquis male utatur eodem lumine, aut non fecerit quod in se est; qui gratiae evasit particeps, habet a se justam gloriandi materiam, quia suo arbitrio seipsum discrevit ab eo, a quo speciali aliquo dono Divinae misericordiae non fuit discretus.
